newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VFB STUTTGART V BAYERN MUNICH MATCH TACTICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VFB STUTTGART V BAYERN MUNICH MATCH TACTICS.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of VfB Stuttgart and Bayern Munich who clash in the German first division in Stuttgart on Sunday (kickoff 1800 GMT):

Playing style: Stuttgart look better going forward than defending, although they have conceded only 16 goals in 15 games. Bulgarian Krasimir Balakov operates just behind the key striking pair of Fredi Bobic and Brazilian Giovane Elber with Thorsten Legat (left) and Matthias Hagner (right) likely to work down the flanks against Bayern. Former German international Thomas Berthold is the key defender at the back, although he still has problems with his temperament.

Strengths: Stuttgart's greatest strength is up front where talented Elber can turn a match in seconds with and Euro 96 striker Bobic is an expert at poaching goals. They have scored more goals at home (22 in 7 games) than any other team.

Motivation - A 50,000-plus crowd should give the home side an extra boost in the south German derby. With just two games remaining before the Bundesliga takes its winter break in December, a victory over Bayern will give Stuttgart a crucial psychological advantage. In the past the team the leading at the halfway stage has often won the championship.

Probable line-up with shirt numbers: 1-Franz Wohlfahrt, 17-Marco Grimm, 5-Frank Verlaat, 4-Thomas Berthold, 7-Matthias Hagner, 20-Zvonimir Soldo, 16-Gerhard Poschner, 3-Thorsten Legat, 10-Krasimir Balakov, 9-Giovane Elber, 11-Fredi Bobic

Playing style: On the surface, typically German with a libero, two out-and-out defenders at the back and versatile midfielders down the flanks who can defend and attack. But coach Giovanni Trapattoni, one of the great thinkers in the game, adds a few Italian touches to the tactics and Bayern are flexible. Midfielder Mario Basler is normally also active down the right flank and has shown good form lately. Veteran Lothar Matthaeus normally operates as libero but Trapattoni may decide to put him back into midfield.

Strengths: After the return of defender Thomas Helmer and wing back Christian Ziege following injuries Bayern are a much stronger team. Striker Alexander Zickler has also impressed national coach Berti Vogts who says he is the perfect partner for Juergen Klinsmann. The club's main problem has always been controversy in the dressing rooms.

Motivation: Bayern have won in Stuttgart for the past two seasons. They know the importance of leading the table at the start of the winter break. Chairman Franz Beckenbauer has been turned up the heat from the boardroom in the past few weeks.

Probable line-up with shirt numbers: 1-Oliver Kahn, 10-Lothar Matthaeus, 15-Samuel Kuffour, 5-Thomas Helmer, 7-Mario Basler, 16-Dieter Hamann, 8-Thomas Strunz, 6-Christian Nerlinger, 17-Christian Ziege, 18-Juergen Klinsmann, 21-Alexander Zickler.
